measured_summary: a real FRB (250924mptq) replayed from recorded voltages lands on the same pixel and DM trial as in 1x, at S/N x1.84. The injection campaign (72 buckets, 0.13-16.8 ms, DM 150-2900) follows the model's recovered fraction with one constant (94% within 20%). Injections now hit their target S/N in normal running; an evening S/N inflation is under investigation (incidents).
status_summary: Observing in 2x at DEC +16.27 (el 69.04). Cutouts were fixed and redeployed at 19:53 UTC. C3's guard against empty cutouts waits for a 'git pull' on h23 and a dsart_c3 restart. Read the incidents section: 28 real events lost their voltages to C3 on empty cutouts. The first calibrator transit on the new data is 2253+161 at ~03:26 UTC on 11-10; the pipeline should then produce new beamformer weights for you to apply.
campaign_text: 72 (DM, width) buckets were probed: DM 150-2900 across both tiers x 8 widths, 0.13-16.8 ms (4-512 native samples), 15:37-18:40 UTC on 11-09, each probe at the same fluence. The calibration factor K = S/N x sqrt(width) / fluence is proportional to the fraction of ideal S/N the search recovers. So, scaled by one constant, the measured K should follow the model's curves; it is a direct test of the whole loss chain. It does: 94% of the 72 buckets lie within 20% of the model (16-84% range 0.91-1.11), across 0.13-16.8 ms and DM 150-2900. That includes the drop at the tier boundary (DM 1600) for bursts shorter than 1 ms. The 16.8 ms buckets and the late 8.4 ms ones were first probed at 18:00-18:40, as the evening S/N inflation set in (incidents), and read ~2x high. They were re-measured after the 19:53 restart, as were five buckets whose probe took K from an early, weaker match. After the restart, a check at DM 500 (fixed position, two shots per point) read S/N within 10% of the K prediction at 0.13, 0.52 and 4.2 ms (S/N 18-25); bursts below S/N ~9 were not detected, as expected. A validation grid on the re-measured buckets, at target S/N 20, read 14-27 (one probe per bucket gives K to roughly +-25%). The grid phase that followed (one shot per bucket at a target S/N 20, 18:40-19:52) came out 1.4-14x too bright. It was not the calibration: the same requests after the 19:53 restart gave S/N 19-21 for target 20 (incidents: S/N inflation). The calibration (K per bucket) is stored for the injection bot.
gain_caption: Model S/N gain of 2x over 1x vs burst width for three DM bands (blue). Orange: the ratio of the 2x K to the last 1x K of the same (DM, width) bucket, labelled by DM. The 1x values were measured on other days (gains, pointing, flagging differ); read the spread, not individual points.
realtime_text: Snapshot of the x2 health page in production, 2026-11-09 ~17:15 UTC, two hours after the start. Every correlator node and every search half is inside its real-time gate with wide margin. The only red entry is RX loss on n01/n02 (4-7e-4), which is the known fault on 2-3 fabric paths into those nodes. It was present before 2x, and fan-in absorbs it.
compromises: Corner-turn format: 4-bit gridded cells with four sub-bands (gridded ns4 cint4), about 0.6% of S/N. You chose it on 2026-10-29 from the measured network capacity. It recovers 0.994 of the dedispersion model and needs 14 Gb/s of clean ingress per search node, the most network margin of the candidates. The heaviest cells travel at 8 bits so bright bursts do not clip. Even so, the 2x wire costs less S/N than the 1x wire, which lost 1.2%.

Four sub-bands in stage 1 (n_sub 4): under 0.5% of S/N on average, up to 1.7% for narrow bursts at DM 100-500. This halves the stage-1 kernel's cost. It was the plan's first fallback for the correlator budget.

0.52 ms, not 0.26 ms. 4x resolution is network-bound: corner-turn traffic grows as 1/T^2, and the fabric cannot carry it without the on-board 10G ports. As a result the legacy-style single-stage search is still ahead below 0.5 ms at low DM (0.70 vs 0.52 of ideal at 0.2 ms).

DM 1600-3000 is searched at 1.05 ms (tier B). Bursts narrower than ~1 ms lose ~25% there, as the injections confirm. Searching it at 0.52 ms would double tier B's cost. At those DMs intra-channel smearing and scattering usually broaden bursts past 1 ms anyway.

The detector amplitude regime is carried over from 1x unchanged. That means input clip 250 sigma, sigma floors, and the injection saturation guard at 240. S/N is linear only up to ~35 sigma and rails at ~250 x sqrt(width). The 2026-07-22 attempt to change it produced an all-night RFI storm, so linearity was left out of scope by decision.

Trial spacing tolerance 1.25. Midway between two DM trials a narrow burst loses up to 1/sqrt(1.25), about 11%; the average loss over DM is a few percent. This is the plan's op-point and is included in the model curves.

A 20 s raw ring instead of cube files. Cutouts must be copied out of the ring within ~11 s of C2's request, and the producer now copies at accept time. A window that has already rotated out is reported TOO_LATE rather than archived.

The fabric's packet loss into n01/n02 is absorbed, not fixed. 2-3 of the 64 paths into those nodes lose ~3e-3 (node totals 4-7e-4) because of a faulty inter-switch link. Data-time fan-in (60 of 64 streams) means it never stalls the search; the S/N cost is ~0.05%.

The web-UI arm epoch is rounded down to the 32-sample grid by corr_fast, and the search mirrors the rounding. Labels stay exact. Rounding `compute_arm_seq` itself would change 1x too, so it was left alone.

Plan steps not done as written. The 1x/2x web-UI drill was dropped, because you asked for 2x to be the only option. The >= 12 h soak is the production run itself, since 15:13 UTC on 11-09. The science validation grid was replaced by the injection calibration campaign, which covers more DMs and all eight filter widths.
fixed_in_deploy: Voltage dumps wrote 0 blocks. 2x candidate times are absolute SNAP-epoch sample numbers, but voltage_retention expected capture-relative ones. It now converts them (--event-specnum-epoch snap); ring block 0 is the first armed page.
The Sky-tab export crashed on the 2x sky object (an attribute only 1x has). Fixed by duck-typing.
The etcd read-back check failed on configs with integer keys. The canonical hash now normalises through a JSON round trip.
The restart helper armed too early. It matched old 'ready' lines in appended child logs. It now arms only after every ready sentinel is newer than the Start.
Search start-up seek. The first live fleet run lagged at attach. The engines now run two throwaway cycles on in-memory data first (priming).
The injection campaign's probe saturated at DM 150, width 4 (S/N 516 > rail). The probe is now repeated once at a fluence scaled to S/N ~40.
operating: Start / stop: web UI Control tab. Start offers only 2x (2x-gridded-ns4-cint4). Use 're-apply op-point' after any config push. Arm only after every corr node has written a fresh ready sentinel (/tmp/dsart-corr-fast-*.ready, a few minutes after Start). The child logs are appended, so an old 'ready' line there does not count.

Updating node code: Control tab, update_dsart, branch x2/main, force on. Never leave the branch blank: blank resets the nodes to origin/main, which is the 1x code. The h23 live checkout is on branch x2-live tracking origin/x2/main; 'git pull' there updates C2/C3/dashboard code (restart the unit or the dashboard afterwards).

Changing configs: edit configs/opoints/2x/*.yaml, then run tools/ops/push_dsart_to_etcd.py --opoint 2x-gridded-ns4-cint4 --plan /home/ubuntu/data/dm_plans/dm_plan_tiered_ns4.npz --write. C2/C3/the inject bot read the yaml from the h23 checkout, so 'git pull' there and restart them.
After a SNAP restart: tools/x2/snap_capture_check.py replaces the Grafana drop-counter check. It captures packets on every corr node and reports per-SNAP sequence offsets and drop rates.

Health: the dashboard's x2 health page (/api/x2/health) shows correlator block time, per-half GPU duty, cube rate, per-node RX loss and cutout latency against the real-time gates. n01/n02 show a loss 'FAIL' at 4-7e-4; that is the known fabric fault, not the search.

Injections: the bot injects at a requested S/N using per-(DM, width) calibration K from this campaign. Widths 4-512 native samples (0.13-16.8 ms), DMs 150-2900. Re-run tools/x2/inject_campaign.py --phase calibrate after any change to gains, beamformer weights or the detector.
New beamformer weights: as you planned, restart with the new weights once a good calibration is in (Stop, update weights, Start with re-apply, arm).
open_items: Find the S/N inflation. Look in the overnight sigma log and the reference shots for the onset, and check the Layer-1 / Layer-2 noise estimates against the 2026-09-23 sigma-feedback flood class. Until it is understood, a restart resets it. The search halves' sigma history is not in Influx (the 1x search_rt_noise measurement has no 2x writer); add it to the pusher.

Pull C3's fail-open guard on h23 (git pull in the live checkout, then systemctl --user restart dsart_c3). Until then C3 still REJECTs on an empty cutout; empty cutouts should no longer occur after the 19:53 fix.

C2 needs a 2x retune. In the first 2.2 h of 2x, C2 dumped 32 real events (~15 per hour; 1x: 3-4.5 per hour). 23 of them were at DM 100-200 with S/N 11-15, i.e. faint, low-DM and impulsive, the RFI signature. Another 126 were suppressed by the rate limiter. 2x searches ~4x the trials at twice the rate with 1x's 11-sigma narrow trigger. Proposed: raise the bar for DM < 300 at narrow widths, checking the change against the injection completeness measured here.

Raw-window retention needs your decision. Each real C2 event archives ~9 GB of raw corner-turn data (all DMs, +-0.5 s) under /dataz/dsa110/candidates/<event>/raw. Nothing prunes it, and /dataz has ~2.3 TB free. Options: keep N days, keep only C3-KEEP events, or archive only for bright classes. Raw windows written 11-09 15:36-19:54 hold only invalid (lapped) rows and could be deleted.
Fabric fault into n01/n02: check the Arista inter-switch/LAG member error counters. 2-3 paths per node lose ~3e-3 because of CRC errors, and the faulty paths change with flow hashing.
Search nodes' antennas.out is not refreshed by calibration pushes. If a calibration ever changes the E/N header, every 2x stream arrives PATTERN_MISMATCH and the search goes blind (fail-loud).
Verify C3 on 2x cutouts now that they arrive in time, and check its R-rule thresholds in ms / DM density against a few days of real events.
4x resolution needs the corr nodes' on-board eno2 10G ports as a second corner-turn path (a slot move does not help).
Merge x2/main into main after your review. The nodes and h23 run x2/main today.

Voltage dumps collide. The corr-node writer is serial and the voltage ring holds ~25 s, so the second of two dumps a few seconds apart loses its window (261109svej: 0 bytes written; the first dump took ~27 s). At 2x's dump rate this happens in every storm. Write dumps concurrently, or copy the window first and write it afterwards, as the cutouts now do.
The calibration endpoint takes K from the first injection match. For 5 of 73 probes a weaker early match set K 2.6-3.7x low (re-measured). Have it wait for the settled best match.

C3 throughput. C3 handles one event at a time and a KEEP waits for voltage collection and a filterbank (~10-20 min), so it manages a few events per hour, while 2x dumps ~15 real events per hour plus injections. On 11-09 evening it had a 10-event backlog. Retuning C2 (above) helps; also consider running voltage collection and filterbanks off the decision path, and taking events oldest first rather than alphabetically.

incidents: 28 real events lost their voltage dumps (11-09 15:49-19:52 UTC). Every cutout after the first arrived empty (next item), and C3 (flag_only off) applied its rules to the all-zero planes, firing no-peak, image-offset, DM-edge and cube-unconfirmed. It REJECTed 28 real events, broadcast deletion of their staged voltages and deleted their raw windows. Most were the low-DM storm pattern (DM 120-180, S/N 11-25), but not all: 261109boeh (DM 753), grgx (DM 1119), jbbq (S/N 19.4, DM 386) and ayay (DM 1524). The voltages cannot be recovered. Fixed: C3 now fails open (KEEP) when the trigger cutout holds no valid rows (commit 8c5087a; needs 'git pull' on h23 and a dsart_c3 restart). Six events dumped just before the fix still had empty cutouts and were waiting for C3; their cutouts were moved aside (cutouts_lapped_empty), so C3 keeps them.

Every cutout from 15:36 to 19:54 was empty. Each request took ~146 s and requests arrived faster, so every search half stayed backlogged. A request's rows were read only when it was served, by which time the 20 s raw ring had overwritten them. The reader marks such rows invalid and nothing errors. The ~9 GB raw window archived per event in that period holds invalid rows only. Fixed and deployed at 19:53 (6209579, 7e2f11b). First event after: cutouts in 27-32 s, all rows valid.

S/N inflation in the evening. Injections at a fixed fluence read normal S/N from 15:30 to 17:30 and after the 19:53 restart. From about 18:00 to 19:52 they read 1.4-14x high, depending on width: for example a 0.52 ms burst at DM 1000 read S/N 84 against 21 after the restart. That is about 3 h after the start. Real events in that window were judged on inflated S/N too. The cause is not yet known; a slow drift in the detector's noise normalisation is the leading suspect. Every half's per-DM sigma is being logged each minute overnight (x2_sigma_log_20261109.jsonl), with a fixed reference injection every 30 min (x2_reference_shots_20261109.jsonl), both in /dataz/dsa110/operations/inject/.
k_shape_caption: Measured injection K per (DM, width) bucket divided by one fitted constant K0 (orange), against the model's recovered fraction of ideal S/N for the deployed 2x search (blue), one panel per injected burst width (Gaussian FWHM). The vertical line is the tier boundary at DM 1600.
gain_text: The same fit for the 1x calibrations (30 buckets measured on several days before 11-08, against the 1x model) gives 2x / 1x = ~1.83 (1.8-1.9) in S/N per unit injected fluence, on top of the model's ratio. The 1x calibrations scatter more around their model (63% within 20%), and they come from other days, pointings and gains, so this factor is indicative only. It has the same size as the one same-data comparison, FRB 250924mptq (x1.84 measured against x1.25 modelled). Both say 2x recovers more, relative to 1x, than the model's dedispersion and sampling terms alone predict. The replay attributes the extra to 1x's lossy 8-bit corner turn for bright bursts.
